Technical Support Portal — User Guide
For: All staff and contractors
Maintained by: Workplace Systems Team
The Workplace Systems Team has launched a single online intake channel for everyday technology needs, and every worker should use it before contacting us any other way. --[1]--.
Previously, colleagues reached us by telephone or messaged a team member directly, and cases often sat in one inbox or were forgotten between shifts. The portal was built to replace that scattered pattern: routine tickets are now logged, timestamped, and routed to the correct specialist automatically, without a person on our side deciding where they should go. --[2]--. Staff and contractors still see the same team behind the scenes, but the intake path has changed. Before you submit your first request, please review the short summary below, which brings the basics of the new system together in one place.
The portal at a glance
Access point: the Help link on the staff home page
Eligible users: all staff and contractors with a company login
Request types: system access, equipment, and account changes
Expected response: within two business days for standard cases
Escalation: call the Workplace Systems Team support line
To start, open the portal from the Help link and choose one of the categories listed above. Selecting the wrong category is the most common reason a case is delayed, so pause to match your issue to the closest label before you continue. --[3]--. Once the form is complete, submit it; the system returns a reference number on screen, and you can enter that number on the Status page at any time to see the latest update.
One situation should not be handled through the portal. If a single fault is stopping several people from working at the same time, telephone the support line right away instead of filing a ticket. --[4]--. Personal messages to individual team members are still discouraged for any request, urgent or not, because they bypass the record we rely on to track workload.
For questions, write to the Workplace Systems Team.

THE RIVERSIDE COMMUNITY BULLETIN
Local Business
Marden Trust Reorganizes Branch Services
By Dana Whitmore, Staff Reporter
Marden Trust Bank has changed the way customers are served at its Cranbrook Avenue Branch. Instead of lining up at a single counter for every request, visitors are now directed to separate zones according to the type of help they need. A notice about the arrangement was posted in the lobby on Monday morning.
Branch manager Colette Duarte said the change followed months of customer surveys showing that shared waiting lines were the main source of complaints. "People waiting to deposit a check were often held up behind those with longer requests," she said. "Separating our services means each visit moves more quickly."
Under the new arrangement, loan officers no longer share the main floor with tellers. Customers seeking a personal loan or a mortgage now sit down with an officer in a private room away from the counters. Everyday account tasks have also been grouped together: opening a new personal account and registering for online banking are now handled at one welcome point rather than at two different desks.
Ms. Duarte encouraged customers to check the printed directory near the entrance, or to ask a floor assistant, before deciding where to wait.

Notice: Lounge entry has changed.
Entry lines grew long at busy hours, so we added self-service. To enter this way, book online for an access code, then hold it at the self-scan reader on arrival and keep your boarding pass ready.
The self-service option works best for a single visitor with a standard boarding pass. Group bookings, guests needing assistance, and non-standard tickets should use the Assistance Desk.
Before launch, our team ran the process for two weeks. We invited regular visitors to enter the private work booths using the self-scan readers. We timed how long each entry took, and the average was far quicker than before, so the procedure is now permanent.
